title: How many continuing education hours do Florida real estate licensees need?
description: Florida real estate CE: 14 hours each renewal with 3 hours Core Law and 3 hours Business Ethics, post-licensing before first renewal, and FREC exam rules.
shortAnswer: Florida real estate brokers, broker associates and sales associates must complete at least 14 hours of continuing education, in hours of 50 minutes, in each renewal period after their first, under section 475.182 of the Florida Statutes and Florida Real Estate Commission (FREC) rule 61J2-3.009. The 14 hours comprise the 3 hour Core Law course, the 3 hour Business Ethics course and at least 8 hours of specialty courses. Before the first renewal, licensees complete post-licensing education instead.
keyTakeaways: Section 475.182 requires at least 14 classroom hours of 50 minutes each during each biennium of a license period for an active license to be renewed.
Rule 61J2-3.009 splits the 14 hours into 3 hours of Core Law, 3 hours of Business Ethics and at least 8 hours of specialty education, and applies to inactive as well as active licensees.
Taking Core Law or Business Ethics in each year of the renewal period earns 3 extra specialty hours per course, which can reduce the separate specialty hours needed.
Before the first renewal, sales associates complete up to 45 hours and brokers up to 60 hours of post-licensing education; a license is null and void if this is not completed.
Commission-prescribed CE requires a grade of 80% or higher on the course exam, and classroom completion requires attendance of at least 90% of the hours.
jurisdiction: United States (Florida): Chapter 475, Part I, Florida Statutes, and Florida Administrative Code chapter 61J2-3
regulator: Florida Real Estate Commission (FREC), within the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation (DBPR)
appliesTo: Real estate sales associates and broker associates
Inactive licensees, who must also meet CE under rule 61J2-3.009
Newly licensed sales associates and brokers, who must complete post-licensing education
Real estate schools, colleges and approved providers delivering CE and post-licensing courses

sections.heading: What does Florida law require for real estate continuing education?

blocks.text: Florida law makes continuing education a condition of renewing an active license. Section 475.182(1)(a) of the [2026 Florida Statutes](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0475/Sections/0475.182.html) requires the renewal application for an active broker, broker associate or sales associate license to include proof that the licensee has completed at least 14 classroom hours of 50 minutes each of continuing education during each biennium of a license period, as prescribed by the Commission.

The same section allows equivalent courses and approved distance learning to substitute hour for hour, and bars the Commission from requiring a centrally monitored written exam for distance courses. Under section 475.182(1)(b), the Commission may accept attendance at one legal agenda session of the Commission as a substitute for 3 classroom hours once per renewal cycle, provided the licensee gives the division at least 7 days' notice.

FREC rule [61J2-3.009](https://www.flrules.org/gateway/ruleNo.asp?id=61J2-3.009) (effective December 22, 2020) divides the requirement into prescribed and specialty courses. Licensees must take the 3 hour Core Law course once in each renewal period and, for licenses expiring on September 30, 2018 or later, the 3 hour Business Ethics course once in each renewal period. Together those give 6 hours, and specialty courses must total at least 8 hours.

blocks.title: Primary text: Rule 61J2-3.009(2)(b)
blocks.text: "Licensees who complete the Core Law course and Business Ethics course will receive 6 hours credit toward the 14 hour requirement. The 'specialty' course hours must total at least 8 hours."

The rule applies to persons holding active or inactive licenses, during each renewal period excluding the first renewal period of their current license. Active members in good standing of The Florida Bar who are otherwise qualified are exempt from the CE rule.

sections.heading: What do new Florida licensees need before their first renewal?

blocks.text: New licensees complete post-licensing education rather than the 14 hour CE before their first renewal. Rule [61J2-3.020](https://www.flrules.org/gateway/ruleNo.asp?id=61J2-3.020) requires everyone who passes a broker or sales associate exam to complete a Commission-prescribed post-licensing course before the first renewal following initial licensure: up to 45 hours of 50 minutes for a sales associate, and up to 60 hours for a broker, inclusive of examination.

The consequence of missing it is severe. Section 475.17 of the [Florida Statutes](https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0400-0499/0475/Sections/0475.17.html) states that the license of any sales associate, and of any broker, who does not complete the postlicensure education requirement before the first renewal following initial licensure "shall be considered null and void." The statute lists eligible subject areas, ranging from property management and finance to business planning and time management for sales associates, and advanced appraisal, commercial brokerage and brokerage office operations for brokers.

Post-licensing courses must be training oriented and build on pre-licensing knowledge, according to rule 61J2-3.020(2), with an emphasis on skills needed to operate effectively and protect the public.

sections.heading: What counts as completing a Florida CE course?

blocks.text: Completion is defined by attendance and exam results, not just enrollment. Rule 61J2-3.009 sets the standards that providers apply.

items: A classroom completion notice may be issued only to a licensee who attended at least 90% of each classroom hour of Commission-prescribed instruction.
A grade of 80% or higher on the Commission-prescribed course exam is satisfactory completion. A student who fails must repeat the course before retaking a different exam form.
A classroom hour is 50 minutes of instruction excluding breaks; live streaming counts as classroom delivery only when students attend at permitted or approved school locations.
Distance course exams need at least 30 items (or 10 for modules of 5 hours or less), with at least 70% of questions at the application level or higher.
An instructor may count a course they teach toward their own CE, but only once per renewal cycle.

blocks.text: Section 475.182(2) to (4) also sets the renewal machinery: the department must provide for renewal at least every 4 years, a license not renewed reverts to involuntary inactive status, and the department mails a notice 60 days before the end of the license period.

sections.heading: How should a Florida brokerage track CE and post-licensing?

blocks.text: A brokerage should track whether each licensee is in their first license period, because that decides whether post-licensing or the 14 hour CE applies, and because missed post-licensing voids the license. The table below is an illustrative template, not a DBPR form.

blocks.text: For the general method, see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) and [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit). Multi-state brokerages can compare [Texas real estate continuing education](/regulations/texas-real-estate-continuing-education), which also runs on a two-year cycle but with more prescribed hours.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can map a brokerage's own escrow, disclosure and agency procedures to assessable outcomes, so the knowledge covered in Core Law is tested against how the brokerage actually operates. Post-licensing deadlines sit in the same record as internal onboarding, so the first renewal is never a surprise. See [professional services](/industries/professional-services).

faqs.q: Do inactive Florida real estate licensees need continuing education?
faqs.a: Yes. Rule 61J2-3.009 applies to all persons holding active or inactive licenses as brokers or sales associates, who must complete the 14 hours in each renewal period after the first. Keeping CE current while inactive avoids extra requirements when the licensee wants to return to active status.

faqs.q: Can a Florida licensee get CE credit for attending a FREC meeting?
faqs.a: Section 475.182(1)(b) allows the Commission to accept attendance at one legal agenda session as a substitute for 3 classroom hours, once per renewal cycle. The licensee must notify the division at least 7 days in advance and cannot earn credit if attending as a party to a disciplinary action.

faqs.q: What happens if a new Florida sales associate misses post-licensing education?
faqs.a: Under section 475.17, the license of a sales associate who does not complete the postlicensure education before the first renewal following initial licensure is considered null and void. The same rule applies to brokers. In practice the person would need to requalify rather than simply renew late.

faqs.q: Do Florida lawyers need real estate CE?
faqs.a: Rule 61J2-3.009(6) exempts active members in good standing of The Florida Bar who are otherwise qualified under the real estate license law from the continuing education requirements of the rule.

factCheck.claim: Section 475.182(1)(a): active broker, broker associate or sales associate renewal requires at least 14 classroom hours of 50 minutes each during each biennium of a license period; (1)(b) legal agenda session substitutes for 3 hours once per renewal cycle with 7 days notice; (2) renewal at least every 4 years; (3) unrenewed licence reverts to involuntary inactive; (4) notice 60 days before end of period. Same text in the 2026 Florida Statutes.

Rule 61J2-3.009 (effective 12/22/2020): 14 hours of 50 minutes for active or inactive licensees each renewal period excluding first; 3 hour Core Law once per period; 3 hour Business Ethics for licences expiring September 30, 2018 or later; taking either each year earns 3 specialty hours; specialty at least 8 hours; specialty courses approved for 2 to 8 hours for 24 months.

Rule 61J2-3.009: 90% classroom attendance for completion notice; 80% exam grade; distance exam minimum 30 items or 10 for modules of 5 hours or less; at least 70% application level; Florida Bar members exempt; instructors may claim a course once per cycle.

Rule 61J2-3.020 (effective 3/25/2018): post-licensing before first renewal; sales associate not exceeding 45 hours, broker not exceeding 60 hours, of 50 minutes each inclusive of exam; courses training oriented.

Section 475.17(3) and (4): postlicensure education up to 45 hours (sales associate) and 60 hours (broker); licence of a sales associate or broker who does not complete it before first renewal shall be considered null and void; lists eligible subjects.
